# Task 86d: settle before marking an upload failed (branch fix/upload-settle-first)

In server/uploads/state.ts, failUploadJob saves status "failed" BEFORE
settleSpendOnce, so a kill or Redis error between the two leaks the hold on the
shared spend counter (and the daily uploads key) forever, and reconcileStaleJobs in
server/uploads/cleanup.ts only looks at "working" jobs. Fix:

   quota refund), and only then save status "failed". Keep exactly-once semantics
   via the existing upload:refunded:<id> marker (uploadRefundKey).
2. cleanup cron: also settle "failed" jobs that have no upload:refunded:<id> marker
   (same tally as failUploadJob, idempotent; never touch "done" jobs).

   status save happens but settle was interrupted is later settled by the cron
   exactly once; failUploadJob order (settle before save) is observable, e.g. a KV
   fake whose set of the job throws still leaves the spend settled.

15|Take the first option that fully works:
16|

90|- A chapter holds several scenes. Each scene has its own emotion.
91|- Paragraph ids carry a global ordinal `n`. Compare `n`, never id strings.

95|- Music is about 15 tracks, pre-generated offline with MusicGen on Modal as one coherent soundtrack: same orchestra and instrumentation, same leitmotif style. 96|- The player picks the track nearest to the scene vector, by cosine similarity over the vector plus intensity and tempo. Hysteresis stops it from flipping on small changes. Skip or change track overrides until the next scene.
97|- The owner listens to short clips before any full generation. Agents do not run Modal until the owner says so.
98|- MusicGen weights are CC-BY-NC. The hackathon demo is non-commercial. The generated tracks must say so in their README.
99|- Chat is low priority and simple. The context is the book text up to the reader's current position. The book prefix goes first and the question goes last, so readers share the prompt cache. Oz is about 55k tokens.
100|- The chat system prompt answers only from the provided text. It refuses knowledge beyond it, even if the model knows the book.
101|- A spoiler mode toggle is for readers who finished the book. It sends the whole text so they can ask about later events. No live Glimmer spoiler guard. No per-chapter summaries for chat. Citing passages is optional.
102|- Glimmer (open weights) keeps a pipeline role. Current decision: it writes the per-scene "why this music" explanation shown in the Developer View.
103|- Spikes come before feature code. Throwaway scripts in `scripts/spikes/` measure Muse Image (response format, latency, Denslow-style prompt), Meta `json_schema` structured output, and the Jev vector on a few Oz scenes. Results go to `docs/spikes.md`.
104|- Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars. Reserve with Redis `INCRBY` before each model call and refund with `DECRBY` after. Reserve per call, including retries.
105|- The server clamps every model tool argument. Tool arguments are untrusted input.
106|- The CSP allows `challenges.cloudflare.com` (script and frame) and `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` (images).
107|- The "Picture this" cache key is the book plus the selection's paragraph range plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`. A selection that overlaps a cached range in the same scene with paragraph Jaccard at least 1/3 reuses that image; a much larger, smaller, or disjoint one gets its own. The prompt is built from the selected paragraphs plus scene context.
108|- Chapter panels (one comic page per chapter) are drawn only for chapters the reader has reached: requests carry `reachedCh` and the server refuses `ch > reachedCh`. It is the client's claim, since there is no server-side reading position.
109|- The "Picture scene" cache key is the book plus the scene id plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`.
110|- Images live in Vercel Blob at deterministic public paths (`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An index in Upstash Redis maps key to Blob URL so hits are one Redis GET; on an index miss check the Blob path with `head()` before generating and backfill the index. Routes return Blob URLs, never image bytes.
111|- Modal endpoints require proxy auth. Tokens live only in env.
112|
113|## Security rules
114|
115|Summary. The full rules live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
116|
117|- Secrets live only in env vars: `.env.local` locally (gitignored), Vercel env vars in prod.
118|- `.env.example` holds names only, never values.
119|- Never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for a secret. Only public ids such as the Turnstile site key may use it.
120|- `core/` stays pure: no keys, no env reads, no network clients, no `server-only`. Key-holding clients live in `server/` (Next.js only, each file starts with `import 'server-only'`) and in `pipeline/` (Node scripts that read env). Callers inject them into `core` functions as arguments. Tests run `core` with fake clients.
121|- The pre-commit secret scan must pass. Never bypass it with `--no-verify`.
122|- Errors to the client are generic. Details go to server logs only, never with keys.
123|- Never log request headers.
124|
125|## Writing rules
126|
127|Run docs, UI copy, and commit messages through the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji in headings, none of seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Headings use sentence case. Commit messages use an imperative subject under 72 chars, and the body says why.
128|
129|## Design
130|
131|Minimalist, functional, elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections.
132|
133|The palette comes from Meta's brand. Meta blue `#0866FF` is the single accent, `#0064E0` for hover and pressed states. Text is near-black `#1C2B33`. Surfaces are white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`. Dark mode keeps the same accent on a near-black surface: `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text.
134|
135|The layout is typography-first. The book sits centered with a comfortable measure, about 60 to 70 chars per line. The companion chat lives in a quiet side panel. Whitespace is generous, the accent color is single, motion is subtle: under 200 ms, and it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
136|
137|These values live as CSS custom properties in [app/tokens.css](app/tokens.css), which is the source of truth.
138|
139|## Hooks
140|
141|`npm install` (or `npm run prepare`) points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. The `pre-commit` hook rejects staged files over 5000 tokens and staged secrets. The `prepare-commit-msg` hook adds the co-author trailer. Run the checks by hand with `npm run check:size` and `npm run check:secrets`, and the hook tests with `npm run test:hooks`.

1|# Upload processing API
2|
3|Server path turning a browser-parsed EPUB into reader data. The browser
4|parses the file with `core/epub.ts` and POSTs the sections; the server
5|cleans, segments, and classifies one chapter-part per call so every
6|request finishes inside the Hobby 60 s budget.
7|
8|## Create
9|
10|`POST /api/uploads`, JSON body:
11|
12|```json
13|{ "title": "Middlemarch", "author": "George Eliot", "sections": [RawSection], "turnstileToken": "…" }
14|```
15|
16|`sections` is the `RawSection[]` shape from `core/clean-types.ts`. Limits:
17|50k words free, 400k with a key; 600 sections; 20k chars per block; 4 MB
18|body. BYOK sends its key per call in the `x-byok-key` header (in memory
19|only, never stored). Needs same-origin JSON plus the Turnstile/human
20|cookie flow shared with chat and images.
21|
22|Success: `{ "status": "created", "id": "u-…", "chapters": 24, "parts": 24 }`.
23|The id is a 128-bit capability; free jobs also bind the anon cookie.
24|The cleaning judge gets 25 s inside this request; past that the book
25|keeps its deterministic chapters.
26|
27|## Step
28|
29|`POST /api/uploads/<id>/step`, body `{}` or `{ "chapter": 3 }` with an
30|optional `turnstileToken` when the human cookie expired. Processes the next
31|pending part (segment + emotion) and stores it. BYOK repeats the key header;
32|free repeats the cookies.
33|
34|- `{ "status": "working", "id": "u-…", "done": 3, "total": 24 }` — call again.
35|- `{ "status": "done", "id": "u-…", "done": 24, "total": 24, "costUsd": 0.021 }`
36|  — the analysis is assembled; `costUsd` is the real Meta+Jev cost.
37|
38|Re-driving a finished part or job is idempotent and free. Music needs no
39|step: scenes carry the same `final` emotion vectors Oz has, so the
40|existing track selection scores them unchanged.
41|
42|## Errors
43|
44|`{ "status": "error", "code": "<code>", "message": "…" }`. Codes: `too_long`
45|(use BYOK, 413), `daily_books_reached` (2/day, 429), `daily_budget_reached`
46|(503), `human_required` (403), `bad_request` (400), `unavailable` (503,
47|refunded), `not_found` (404), `expired` (30 days, 410).
48|
49|## Money and quota
50|
51|Free creates hold a sized reserve: 5k micro per part plus 1 micro per
52|word, floored at 50k and capped at 250k micro (a 3,955-word book measured
53|USD 0.0027). The hold reconciles to the real Meta+Jev cost at finalize;
54|each part result carries its own usage so parallel steps lose nothing,
55|and one settle guard keeps the adjustment exactly once. Failed jobs keep
56|what they spent and refund the book quota only when nothing ran. Jobs
57|still working after 6 hours are settled the same way by the daily
58|cleanup. BYOK spends the reader's key but still takes a per-person quota
59|of 10 creates a day; exhaustion answers `daily_books_reached`.
60|
61|## Reading and cleanup
62|
63|`loadUploadedBook(id)` in `server/uploads/loader.ts` returns the
64|`BookPayload` the reader consumes (`{ book, scenes }`). Uploads expire
65|after 30 days; `GET /api/cron/cleanup-uploads` (Bearer `CRON_SECRET`,
66|daily) deletes their private blobs.
67|
68|## Storage
69|
70|Uploads live in a separate private Blob store, not the public image
71|store: a store's access mode is fixed at creation, so `access: "private"`
72|puts would fail against it. The token comes from
73|`UPLOADS_BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` (passed explicitly to every Blob call)
74|and the owner creates the store by hand. Without the token the routes
75|answer `unavailable`; they never fall back to the public store.
